subject: Temporary region override request for compute shift
messages:
From: Jorge Suarez <jorge.suarez@acmehealth.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 27 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Temporary region override for compute shift

Hi Dylan / Marissa,

We're planning a scheduled migration of our analytics batch compute to a new instance type next month. The maintenance window is 2027-11-19 22:00 UTC — 2027-11-20 02:00 UTC (4 hours). To complete the migration without data loss, we need Redwood to allow a temporary compute override so that some processing jobs run in the eu-west-1 region for up to 48 hours (start-of-window plus a short rollback buffer).

Key asks: 
- A narrow, time-bound permission to route compute (not long-term storage) to eu-west-1 for that window.
- Confirmation of encryption-in-transit and at-rest while in the temporary region, and that customer-controlled KMS keys remain in our account.
- Audit logs that show any cross-region data egress and a copy of those logs within 24 hours.
- A short subprocessor/evidence list if any third parties will touch payloads during the window.

We attached a short change window proposal (change-window-proposal.pdf) with the jobs that will be affected. Please let me know required conditions from Redwood's side and whether you need additional paperwork (SLA exception, DPA addendum).

We need a decision by EOD 2027-10-29 to confirm scheduling with our platform team.

Thanks,
Jorge
Cloud Operations Manager
Acme Health

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Jorge Suarez <jorge.suarez@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 27 Oct 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary region override for compute shift

Hi Jorge — thanks for the clear summary and the timeline.

Quick acknowledgement: we can evaluate a time-bound compute override for that exact window, but we have a few non-negotiable conditions to protect residency commitments and controls. I've attached a short note with the conditions I've flagged for approvals (proposed-conditions.txt).

High level:
- We only permit compute to execute outside of the primary storage region if customer-controlled KMS keys remain the authority and we have a signed temporary exception (DocuSign or other).
- All cross-region copies must be ephemeral, with automated deletion within 72 hours of the end of the window.
- Audit logs and tokenized request traces will be shared to the Acme Health Drive folder within 24 hours; we'll redact operational metadata as needed.

Looping in Irene from Security for the detailed checklist. Irene — can you confirm whether the request needs a DPA addendum or if the existing DPA (clause 8.2) plus an exception form will suffice? Also confirm subprocessor vetting we need to provide.

Action items for Acme: share the final job list and the minimum start and end timestamps (UTC). If you can provide a short operational rollback plan we can include it in the approval.

Once we have Security's checklist and the signed exception, I'll route to Ops for a capacity ticket.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

<attachment: proposed-conditions.txt (text, 3KB)>

From: irene_choi@redwood.com <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Jorge Suarez <jorge.suarez@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 27 Oct 2027 12:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary region override for compute shift

Thanks for the ping. Below is the Security checklist we'll require before approving a temporary compute region override. I'm posting it here so Acme has a single action list.

Security checklist (required):
1) Customer-held KMS keys: confirmation that Acme will keep sole custody of the CMK for any transient storage. If Redwood needs to operate a key for the window (only if absolutely necessary), we will require an explicit, time-limited key policy and pre-authorized key access records.
2) Scope: documentation that only compute will run in eu-west-1; primary PII-bearing storage (S3 buckets, object storage) must remain in the US region and cannot be replicated automatically.
3) Ephemeral retention: any temporary replicas or caches must be flagged 'ephemeral' and auto-deleted within 72 hours; retention policy must be codified and signed.
4) Audit & telemetry: per-request audit logs, k8s pod IDs, and egress metrics must be exported to the Acme Drive folder and to our secure audit pipeline (read-only for Acme) within 24 hours of the end of the window.
5) Subprocessor visibility: provide an explicit list of subprocessors and versions (we'll need this to map to our DPA subprocessor list). If any managed services will touch content (e.g., managed transform jobs), list them.
6) IP allowlist & ACLs: Redwood must restrict control plane modifications to a whitelist of Acme ops IPs during the window; emergency access will be documented and routed through our escalation process.
7) Rollback plan: Acme must provide a rollback trigger and an execution plan (how jobs will be stopped and how to verify no residual copies remain).
8) Legal signoff: a signed exception form or short addendum referencing DPA clause 8.2 with the exact timestamps and retention commitments. DocuSign link is preferred.

We can provide a minimal subprocessor roster for the specific jobs — see attached draft (subprocessor-roster.csv) — but we need Acme to confirm which job IDs & data classes are in-scope so we can finalize the list.

If all items above are confirmed and you provide the signed exception, Security will green-light the Ops change ticket. Otherwise, we'll decline the compute override.

Irene Choi
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
